newsitem.title: UGANDA: U.N. team assesses aid in rebel-hit western Uganda.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team assesses aid in rebel-hit western Uganda.

text.p: A United Nations assessment team arrived in a western Uganda town on Wednesday to assess humanitarin needs for over 30,000 people displaced by fighting between government troops and Moslem rebels.

The team led by officials from the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) reached Bundibugyo by military helicopter because more than a week of hit-and-run fighting has cut off the only road leading into the remote town.

A senior army officer told reporters that the Ugandan army was only able to provide security around a one km radius of Bundibugyo which was attacked by Moslem rebels from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Local government official, Wilson Mutabazi, told reporters that as many as 38,000 people in and around Bundibugyo had been displaced by fighting which started 11 days ago.
"We estimate they are many thousands of displaced people here. As many as 38,000. The problem is the displaced and local population are mixed together," Mutabazi said.
WFP deputy country director, Michael Jones, said the food agency would try and deliver some 60 tonnes of food aid to the displaced in Bundibugyo on Thursday.
"We are going to try to get 60 tonnes of food into Bundibugyo from the town of Fort Portal if the road is safe," said Jones.

Senior military officials said they feared people in remote villages, far away from the protection of the government army, were still being attacked and killed by the rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).
Lieutenant-Colonel Charles Angina told reporters that rebels of the ADF were still roaming remote villages at will.
Angina's force, which escorted the U.N. team, brought in Fresh supplies including grenades, mortars and tinned food for government soldiers in Bundibugyo.
On Monday, Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi said that the rebel force had broken into small groups and attacked the town with mortars and the army was fighting to repulse them.

The government-owned New Vision newspaper reported on Monday that up to 300 rebels took part in the attack on Bundibugyo and at least 20 soldiers had been wounded and taken to hospital after the attacks.
